Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): speed up incremental delta streaming and replace preprocessor fingerprinting
Issues.Body:
On incremental rebuilds, `ng-analyze` previously re-streamed every transitively invalidated file even when re-analysis produced an identical `AnalysisResult`. Multi-file `NgModule` chunks also re-serialized full metadata for unchanged peer files whenever one member changed. On the JavaScript side, `HybridCompiler` JSON-serialized and hashed `AnalysisResult` objects, source text, and emitted code to validate cached bindings and `ProcessedFile` outputs. Under `optimize: true`, each component's `AnalysisResult` embeds resolved `.d.ts` declaration metadata, so serializing and hashing those payloads dominated warm rebuild CPU and memory overhead.

This stack tightens incremental invalidation across `ng-analyze` and `HybridCompiler`:

- `QueryContext::analyze_file_wire` polls cached `Shared` futures once on insertion so `Shared::peek` can read evicted entries, and `QueryEngine` separates direct source or resource invalidations from transitive wire cache evictions.
- `AnalysisResult` and its nested wire types derive `PartialEq` and `Eq`, allowing `run_coordinator` to compare recomputed wire outputs against evicted baseline entries and skip re-streaming unchanged transitive dependents.
- Multi-file `NgModule` delta chunks emit lightweight `unchanged: true` stubs for clean peer files and hydrate them from `HybridCompiler`'s cached metadata instead of re-serializing full declaration payloads across IPC.
- `HybridCompiler` replaces string fingerprints with a monotonic per-file `ChangeKind` state (`Unchanged`, `Dependency`, `ResourceOnly`, `Source`) and reference-keyed `ProcessedFileCache` lookups, preserving cached parsed templates across dependency-only updates.

In incremental benchmark suites, wire early cutoff saves 118 to 192 ms on warm `.ts` and `.d.ts` edits, and `unchanged: true` peer stubs save 133 to 222 ms on warm template edits in multi-file `NgModule` chunks. On the JavaScript side, `ChangeKind` and reference-keyed caching eliminate JSON serialization and hashing of `AnalysisResult` payloads and emitted code on incremental passes.

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): extract empty .d.ts ngContentSelectors and skip redundant dependency prefetches
Issues.Body:
External `.d.ts` components without `<ng-content>` emit `never` as the 7th type argument of `ɵɵComponentDeclaration`. `extract_ng_content_selectors_from_type` in `dts.rs` previously returned `None` for non-tuple types, empty tuples, and tuples without string-literal elements. Because `DeclarationMetadata.ngContentSelectors` arrived unset, `DependencyTemplates` treated those `.d.ts` components as unparsed source components, ran `getMetadataForFile` (`AnalyzeFileWire` and `AnalyzeFileSemantic`) on their declaration files, read the `.d.ts` files from disk, and parsed empty templates for each class. `utils::is_dts` in `ng-analyze` and the `.d.ts` checks in the TypeScript pipeline also matched only `.d.ts` rather than `.d.mts` and `.d.cts`. In addition, `DependencyTemplates.prefetch` read `.ts` dependency files from disk when every needed component used `templateUrl` or an indirect `template` expression, and `processFile` ran `prefetch` again even when `prepareChunk` had already bound `preparedTcbData` for the file's current content.

This change aligns `extract_ng_content_selectors_from_type` with `ngtsc`'s `DtsMetadataReader` (`readStringArrayType`) so any present 7th type argument without string-literal tuple elements resolves to `Some(vec![])`, returning `None` only when `ɵɵComponentDeclaration` has fewer than 7 type arguments. `utils::is_dts`, `is_ts_file`, and `is_compilation_root` now delegate to `ModuleFormat::from_path` so `.d.mts` and `.d.cts` files are analyzed as declaration files. On the TypeScript side, `isDeclarationFilePath` and `needsNgContentSelectors` handle `.d.ts`, `.d.mts`, and `.d.cts` consistently across `ngp`, `DependencyTemplates`, `HybridCompiler`, `IncrementalEmitTracker`, `OutOfBandDiagnosticRecorderImpl`, and `processFile`, preventing legacy declaration files without the 7th type argument from triggering emit, template prefetches, or consumer tracking. `DependencyTemplates.prefetch` now reads `.ts` dependency source text only when at least one requested component uses a direct inline template (reusing and caching `FileAnalysis.sourceContent`), and `processFile` skips `prefetch` when `preparedTcbData` is already bound for the current content or when generating an HMR update module.

On a cold optimized build of a component target importing ~30 external UI and CDK `.d.ts` libraries, this reduces filesystem reads from 532 to 425 (-107 reads, -530 KB), cuts `AnalyzeFileWire` and `AnalyzeFileSemantic` queries from 37 to 10 with zero `.d.ts` re-queries, drops `TemplatesParsed` from 80 to 14, and reduces `PrepareChunk` time by ~200 to 320 ms across standalone CLI and persistent sidecar worker runs.

Issues.Title: fix(forms): restore custom control values when a field change is reverted
Issues.Body:
Hi Angular team!!

I reproduced #72065 with a custom input that clears itself on Escape. When a parent handler restores the field’s previous value during the same keypress, the field and the input end up showing different values. This change keeps them in sync.

- [x] Tests for the change have been added.
- [ ] Docs have been added or updated.

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Suppose the field starts at `"Ada"`. Pressing Escape clears the input’s `model()`, then the parent restores the field to `"Ada"`. Angular remembers `"Ada"` as the last value it wrote to the control, so it skips the write that would restore the input. After rendering, the field contains `"Ada"` and the input is empty.

Fixes #72065.

## What is the new behavior?

When the control emits a value that differs from the last value Angular wrote to it, Angular invalidates the cached value for that control. On the next render, it writes the field’s final value back to the input.

This also preserves support for controls with separate `value` and `valueChange` properties. Those controls can emit a change and rely on Angular to write the new value back to their input. Caching the emitted value directly would skip that write.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

I added a regression test that edits the control’s model and restores the field’s previous value before the next render. I also extended the existing test for separate input and output properties to check the value the control actually receives.

The Signal Forms web test suite passed in Chromium and Firefox.

Issues.Title: feat(core): let applications merge the classes of an element before they are written (provideClassMerge)
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

core

### Description

Utility CSS frameworks make two *different* class names conflict: `px-4` from a component's host and `px-2` from the template that uses it both set horizontal padding. Angular applies both, and the winner is decided by the order of the rules in the stylesheet, not by where the classes come from. So a consumer can't reliably override a component's classes.

This is now a mainstream setup: `ng new` offers Tailwind CSS as a stylesheet system and `ng add tailwindcss` configures it. Component libraries built on it (spartan/ui, shadcn-style libraries) all need to resolve these conflicts, usually with `tailwind-merge`.

In other frameworks this is simple because a component receives `className` / `class` as a prop and composes it itself (`cn(own, props.className)`). In Angular the classes of a host element come from sources the component can't see: the consumer's `class` and `[class]` / `[class.x]` bindings, host directives, other directives and `Renderer2`. There is no single place to merge them, so libraries work around it after Angular has written the classes. spartan/ui, for example, does it with `effect`s, a `MutationObserver` per element and suppressing CSS transitions during hydration, because the classes land in two steps and cause flicker. That's ~950 lines (with tests) and a measurable runtime cost.

Angular already knows every class source of an element and their precedence, so it's the natural place to resolve conflicts once, before writing to the DOM.

### Proposed solution

A small, generic, opt-in hook. It isn't Tailwind specific: any function that turns a list of classes into a class string.

```ts
import {provideClassMerge} from '@angular/core';
import {twMerge} from 'tailwind-merge';

bootstrapApplication(App, {
  providers: [provideClassMerge((classes) => twMerge(classes))],
});
```

Semantics:

- Angular passes the classes of an element in its precedence order, lowest first: host directives → component host → other directives (matching order) → template → `Renderer2.addClass`. Within a source: static `class` → `[class]` → `[class.x]` (in template order).
- The merge function is called once per change and the result is written to `class` with a single write.
- SSR and hydration (including incremental hydration) produce the same classes on the server and the client. Server-rendered classes Angular doesn't own are kept until the app is stable, so classes such as `RouterLinkActive`'s don't flicker.
- Classes added with `Renderer2.addClass` (`RouterLinkActive`, `NgClass`) take part in the merge, and `removeClass` restores the class they replaced. Classes added outside Angular (`classList`, `animate.enter`) are kept as they are.
- Tree-shakable: without the provider only an injection token lands in the bundle. `[style]` bindings are untouched.
- The function must be pure and deterministic (results are cached per template location).

### Prototype and numbers

I have a working implementation with tests (acceptance, browser, platform-server hydration, forms), API docs and a guide section: [diff against v21.2.16](https://github.com/angular/angular/compare/v21.2.16...trs-dev-1:angular:prototype/class-merge-hook) (branch `prototype/class-merge-hook` on my fork; I'll rebase it on `main` for a PR). The existing suites pass unchanged. With a global identity merge, the only differences are class order in 8 specs that assert `className` strings.

To validate it, spartan/ui (300 components) was migrated from its userland solution to the hook. Measured on the spartan docs app (Chromium, 4x CPU throttling, median of 7 runs):

| | Userland merging (today) | `provideClassMerge` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Elements with different classes (~46k elements, SSR + hydrated) | – | **0** |
| Script time, `/components/date-picker` | 1637 ms | **531 ms** |
| Total blocking time, `/components/date-picker` | 2982 ms | **1844 ms** |
| Transition flicker on load without suppression (98 routes) | 152 transitions | **0 caused by classes** |
| SSR time per route | 171 ms | 172 ms |

Compared to stock Angular without any merging, on a list of helm-like components: rendering is faster (one `class` write per element instead of one `classList.add` per class), and updates are on par (1k rows: render 57.3 → 49.2 ms, update 13.2 → 12.4 ms).

Known cost: each changed class binding re-merges the element, so an element with N changed bindings is merged N times in one change detection.

### Alternatives considered

- **Userland, after Angular writes the classes** (what libraries do today): needs effects and DOM observation on every element, writes classes twice, and causes transitions during hydration that have to be suppressed.
- **A single `[class]` binding owned by the component** (`hostClass = computed(() => cn(base, consumerClass()))` with a `class` input): it misses classes from other directives, host directives and `Renderer2`, and takes `class` away from consumers as a normal attribute.
- **A compiler-level solution**: the sources are only known at runtime (applied directives, `createComponent({directives})`, `Renderer2`, hydration), so a runtime hook is needed anyway.

I'd be happy to open a PR if the direction looks good to the team.

cc spartan/ui maintainers: @goetzrobin @ashley-hunter @MerlinMoos

Issues.Title: refactor(compiler-cli): add BatchingHost and WASM host request pump protocol
Issues.Body:
Asynchronous bundler integrations cannot resolve specifiers or read module text synchronously inside
Rust, so the WASM analyzer needs a suspend-and-resume host that batches every discoverable request
in a pump wave and resumes parked queries once JavaScript supplies results.

Add BatchingHost and its JSON wire request/result types under ng-analyze/src/host. BatchingHost
queues uncached resolve and load lookups behind shared oneshot receivers so concurrent queries in
the same or overlapping waves share a single request slot, serves proactive virtualFiles and
updateFileContent buffers plus inline ResolveResult code without extra round trips, maps per-slot
error objects to HostError, and ignores late responses for cancelled or unknown batch IDs.

Wire BatchingHost into Analyzer (running over NoopFs and dropping incomplete cached SharedQuery
tasks on cancellation so parked futures never block or poison the cache) and expose hostRequests
events and provide_host_results on WasmAnalyzer after ready metadata and compilation chunks are
drained.

## What is the current behavior?

`benchmark-compare.yml` resolves the pull request head SHA when the job runs and checks out that commit after a team member comments `/benchmark-compare`. That SHA can differ from the head that was present when the comment was written, as described in #58760.

Before checkout, the workflow resolves the commit that was at the PR head when the comment was created. If the head has moved since then, the job fails and asks for a new comment. Checkout uses only that verified SHA.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler-cli): suggest exposing file and global symbols used in templates
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Template and host binding expressions read bare names from the component instance (`foo` is `this.foo`). A template that uses a symbol imported or declared in the component's file, or a global, fails with an error that doesn't explain why:

```ts
import {formatDate} from './util';

@Component({template: '{{ formatDate(value) }}'})
export class MyCmp { value = 1; }
```

```
error TS2339: Property 'formatDate' does not exist on type 'MyCmp'.
```

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

When TS reports a missing property for such an implicit read, the template diagnostic checks whether the name is a value that is imported or declared in the component's file, or a global. If so, it suggests the existing workaround of exposing it on the class:

```
error TS2339: Property 'formatDate' does not exist on type 'MyCmp'. 'formatDate' is imported in this file, but template expressions can only read members of the class. To use it in the template, add it to the class, e.g. 'protected readonly formatDate = formatDate;'.
```

- Covers named, aliased, default and namespace imports, top-level declarations (including ones declared after the class), and globals. Works in templates and host bindings.
- No suggestion for DOM globals (`name`, `open`, `status`, ...), which almost always mean a missing component property. Also none for type-only imports, imported interfaces and types, unknown names, or explicit reads like `value.foo`.
- The module scope is read syntactically (`util/src/module_scope.ts`). The type checker is only used to tell imported values from types and to find globals.

The PR has two commits:
1. ngtsc: the suggestion in `typecheck/src/diagnostics.ts`, wired into the template type checker.
2. ngp: the same suggestion, shared via `getExposeSymbolSuggestion`, applied in ngp's TCB diagnostic translation. The new specs run under both the `ngtsc` and `ngtsc_ngp` targets.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Only the text of an existing error changes.

## Other information

The ngp language service maps tsserver diagnostics without a type checker, so it doesn't add the suggestion yet.

Issues.Title: Support pre-loading on hover
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

router

### Description

When a complex Angular app with lazy-loaded routes has many possible routes that are connected, it is hard to define a `PreloadingStrategy` that does not pre-load too much while keeping the best User Experience / Performance.

Let's say if the courrent route is page /b12 and you can possibly navigate to /b1, /b2, /b3, ... plus /a1, /c1, /d1, /e1... for the best User Experience you might want to preload all those routes, but not routes like /a2, /a3,
This is a lot of routes to pre-load, lots of network requests, and makes the `PreloadingStrategy` implementation bloated.

The best compromise I have seen in fwks so far is SvelteKit's [preload on hover](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/link-options#data-sveltekit-preload-data) where there is nothing to setup for users. In the previous example, it would mean zero pre-loading until the user hovers on of the connected links.

I am aware of the library `ngx-hover-preload` but it relies on either an Angular Module `HoverPreloadModule` or importing `LinkDirective` everywhere `routerLink` is used...

Would you consider including in Angular's default router apis a way to preload on hover?

### Proposed solution

Propose a new `PreloadingStrategy` that supports preload on hover.  
It would most likely involve a `Service` that is injected in the new `PreloadOnHoverStrategy` and optionally injected in `RouterLink`.

### Alternatives considered

We can use `ngx-hover-preload` already, but not a fan of using modules in modern angular or repeating `LinkDirective` imports everywhere we are importing `RouterLink`.

We can also fork the `RouterLink` code and enhance it but that's **very far** from what we want, we highly value using Angular's default apis when we can.

Issues.Title: validateStandardSchema should check for non-optional fields and add required flag to them (for mat-form-field * support)
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

core

### Description

Fields validated with Zod through `validateStandardSchema` do not automatically receive Angular Signal Forms’ `required` metadata. As a result, `mat-form-field` does not display its required-field asterisk (`*`) even when the Zod schema rejects an empty value.

Required metadata should reflect whether a field is optional according to its schema, including nested object and array fields. 

### Proposed solution

Extend the Zod-backed validation wrapper to detect non-optional fields and apply Angular’s `required` rule to their Signal Forms paths.

Use safe parsing of `undefined` to detect optional schemas, since the `isOptional()` method is deprecated and this is the correct alternative. 

### Alternatives considered

- Mark required fields manually in each form, which duplicates schema rules.

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the contribution guidelines.
- [x] A regression test covers the change.
- [ ] Docs have been added or updated.

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Resetting a reactive control and restoring its previous value before the next render can leave a custom input using `transformedValue` blank. The reset callback updates the raw value immediately, while the custom control's model and its last bound value still hold the previous value.

## What is the new behavior?

Write the reset value to the custom control's model and update its last bound value before invoking the reset callback. A subsequent write of the previous value then reaches the model and restores the formatted input.

Fixes #72068.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

- The new regression failed on `main` with an empty input and passed with the fix.
- The Chromium Signal Forms and reactive forms suites passed, as did the Node forms suite and dependency checks.
- Firefox could not start locally because it could not open the test profile. The same launch error occurred on `main` before the change.

Issues.Title: fix(zone.js): only cancel fake timers that fakeAsync scheduled
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #72070

A timer scheduled before `fakeAsync()` (for example the zoneless scheduler's `setTimeout`/`requestAnimationFrame` race armed by `TestBed.createComponent()`) can be cancelled inside `fakeAsync()` through the `ProxyZoneSpec`. `FakeAsyncTestZoneSpec.onCancelTask` then clears whichever fake timer has the same numeric id, so an unrelated fake timer silently disappears and `tick()` never runs it. The real timer is also never cleared natively.

## What is the new behavior?

`FakeAsyncTestZoneSpec` remembers which instance scheduled each macrotask. Cancelling a task it didn't schedule goes to the parent delegate, and a task scheduled by another fake zone is cleared from that zone's queue.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: feat(@angular/compiler): add on-demand incremental rebuild mode (HTTP API & MCP tool) for `ng serve`
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

compiler

### Description

With the rapid adoption of AI coding agents (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Antigravity), the frontend development workflow is shifting. Instead of developers manually editing single files and immediately inspecting changes via HMR/Live Reload, AI agents now perform rapid, multi-file edits in batches before the developer reviews the final result.

Currently, this creates a major bottleneck with `ng serve`:
1. **Default Watch Mode (`ng serve`):** As an AI agent rapidly generates and modifies dozens of files, the dev server continuously triggers incremental rebuilds. This spikes CPU/RAM usage, slows down the entire machine, and causes unnecessary build thrashing mid-generation.
2. **Disabling Watch (`ng serve --watch=false`) or Cold Restart:** Running `ng serve --watch=false` prevents automatic rebuilds, but provides no mechanism to trigger an incremental rebuild afterward. Developers are forced to restart `ng serve`, discarding the in-memory build graph/cache and waiting 3–5 minutes for a full cold build on large enterprise projects.



### Proposed solution

Introduce an on-demand rebuild mode for `ng serve` (e.g., `--on-demand-build` or `--manual-rebuild`) that keeps the dev server and its in-memory incremental build graph alive, **pauses automatic file-system watchers**, and allows external tools/AI agents to explicitly trigger an incremental rebuild once a batch of edits is completed.

**Proposed Workflow:**
1. Start the dev server in on-demand mode:
   ```bash
   ng serve --on-demand-build
   ```
2. The server performs the initial build, caches the dependency graph in memory, and remains idle without reacting to file system events.
3. Once an AI agent finishes its task (or via an agent post-task hook), it triggers an incremental rebuild using either:
   * **Local HTTP Endpoint:**
     ```bash
     curl -X POST http://localhost:4200/__ng_rebuild
     ```
   * **Angular CLI MCP Server (`ng mcp`) Integration:**
     Expose a built-in MCP tool (e.g., `trigger_rebuild` or `rebuild_dev_server`) in `@angular/cli`'s MCP server so AI agents can natively signal the active dev server to compile modified files upon task completion.
4. Angular CLI executes a fast **incremental rebuild** (reusing the existing `ngtsc` and esbuild/Vite in-memory cache) for only the changed files and pushes the update to the browser.

### Alternatives considered

* **Using `ng serve --watch=false`:** Only disables watching after the initial build; lacks any API or signal to trigger subsequent incremental builds without restarting the process.
* **Increasing `poll` interval / debounce time:** Still relies on arbitrary timers rather than deterministic completion signals from AI agents, resulting in premature builds mid-generation or unnecessary waiting afterward.
* **Restarting `ng serve` after AI edits:** Discards the in-memory build cache, incurring a 3–5 minute cold build penalty every time.


### Additional context

Under the hood, esbuild already supports manual incremental rebuilds via `context.rebuild()`, and Vite supports disabling `server.watch`. Decoupling **file change detection** from **incremental compilation triggers** in `@angular/build`—especially when paired with the official Angular CLI MCP server (`ng mcp`)—would fit cleanly into the current architecture and significantly improve hardware efficiency and developer experience (DX) for AI-assisted workflows on large Angular codebases.

Issues.Title: feat(@angular/build): add `manualRebuild` option to the dev-server
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Feature

## What is the current behavior?

`ng serve` either rebuilds on every file change (`watch: true`) or never rebuilds again after the initial build (`watch: false`). When many files are edited in a batch, for example by AI coding agents, the dev server rebuilds over and over while the edits are still in progress. The only other option is `--watch=false` followed by a restart, which throws away the in-memory incremental build state and means a full cold build every time.

Issue Number: angular/angular-cli#34743 (filed against `angular/angular`, but the implementation lives in this repo)

## What is the new behavior?

### `@angular/build`: new `manualRebuild` dev-server option

```bash
ng serve --manual-rebuild
```

- The file watcher keeps running and change sets are merged in the background (add→remove becomes `removed`, remove→add becomes `modified`, and so on). Rebuilds no longer start on their own.
- A rebuild of everything pending, reusing the existing esbuild/ngtsc incremental state, starts when one of these happens:
  - `POST /__ng_rebuild` is sent to the dev server. The response is sent after the rebuild finishes and the results have been pushed to clients:
    ```bash
    curl -X POST http://localhost:4200/__ng_rebuild
    # {"status":"success"}   (or "failure" | "no-changes" | "cancelled")
    ```
  - `b` is pressed in the terminal (a new Vite CLI shortcut).
- Before a rebuild starts, the server waits until no file events have arrived for a short period (300 ms). This way edits made just before the request are still picked up by the watcher's debounce and included.
- Requests that arrive while a rebuild is running are not resolved by that rebuild. They are handled by the next one, so a `success` response always covers every edit made before the request.
- Browser requests carrying a cross-origin `Origin` header are rejected (403). Methods other than POST get a 405.
- If `watch` is disabled, the option does nothing and a warning is logged.

Implementation notes:
- `utils/manual-rebuild.ts` adds `ManualRebuildController` and `waitForManualRebuilds()`, which gates the watcher's change stream.
- `runEsBuildBuildAction` takes an optional controller (as the internal application option `manualRebuild`) and resolves requests once a rebuild's results have been emitted.
- The dev-server middleware sits at `tools/vite/middlewares/rebuild-middleware.ts`.

### `@angular/cli`: MCP integration

- `devserver_start` accepts `manualRebuild: true`, which starts `ng serve --manual-rebuild`.
- New `devserver_rebuild` tool: an agent calls it once it has finished a batch of edits. It triggers the rebuild through the endpoint above, waits for it, and returns `{ status, logs }`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No

The option defaults to `false`. Default behavior is unchanged.

## Other information

- Tests:
  - `manual-rebuild_spec.ts` (unit): change merging, request gating, the settle window, and cancellation.
  - `dev-server/tests/options/manual-rebuild_spec.ts` (integration): a change is not rebuilt until it is requested, and is served after the request. Also covers `no-changes`, 405 and 403.
  - `devserver_spec.ts`: the MCP start args and the rebuild tool.
- Name and route (`manualRebuild`, `/__ng_rebuild`) are open to bikeshedding.
- This PR does not update docs on angular.dev. I'm happy to send a follow-up if the API is accepted.
- The `pnpm-lock.yaml` on `main` currently fails to parse (`duplicate mapping key: minimatch@11.0.8`), so I ran the tests locally with the previous commit's lockfile. This PR does not touch the lockfile.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): report the failing sequence sub-option in runner args errors
Issues.Body:
The `runnerArgs` validation reports every invalid value for the `--sequence` option with a single message that only lists the supported sub-option names: `--sequence.seed=-1` fails with 'The Vitest "--sequence" option requires only the following options: "--sequence.shuffle", "--sequence.seed".' although the user already used one of those options, and nothing states the actual value requirement.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/pwa): support projects with the pre-v18 src/assets layout
Issues.Body:
`ng add @angular/pwa` decides between the `public` and legacy `src/assets` layouts with `host.exists(assetsDir)`, but `Tree.exists()` only matches files, so the legacy branch never runs and pre-v18 layout projects get the manifest and icons in a `public` directory their build does not serve. The manifest link injected into index.html then 404s and the application is not installable, while the schematic reports success.

Detect the directory through its entries instead and restore the layout that worked before the `public` directory support was introduced: the manifest is written to the source root, where the asset entry added to the workspace configuration and the injected manifest link already point, and the icons are written to the existing `assets` directory with the manifest referencing them as `assets/icons/*`. The workspace file is now written after the asset entry additions, which previously happened after `writeWorkspace()` and were never persisted. Projects using the `public` directory layout are unaffected.

Issues.Title: dev-server keeps stale code of a linked (`file:`) library after `ng-packagr --watch` rebuilds it (rebuild reported, restart required)
Issues.Body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

In a workspace with an application and a separate Angular library linked with a `file:` dependency, rebuilding the library in watch mode makes `ng serve` print "Application bundle generation complete", but the application bundle (`main.js`) still contains the **previous** compiled code of the library. The new code only appears after stopping and restarting `ng serve`.

The source map embedded in the same `main.js` already contains the **new** library source (`sourcesContent`), while the code is the old one. So the updated `.map` file seems to be re-read, but the content of `libreria.mjs` is reused from a previous build.

I could not determine whether this is the in-memory load cache, the file watcher, or something else.

### Minimal Reproduction

**Setup**

- Windows, project and library in sibling folders (`D:\...\proyecto-22` and `D:\...\libreria-22`).
- Library built with `ng build libreria --watch --configuration development` (ng-packagr).
- App `package.json`: `"libreria": "file:../libreria-22/dist/libreria"` (npm `install-links=false`, so `node_modules/libreria` is a Junction to `libreria-22\dist\libreria`).
- `preserveSymlinks` is not set (enabling it is not an option for me: the library sources then resolve under the app's folder and breakpoints in the library do not bind in VS Code).
- `angular.json` of the app:

  ```json
  "build": {
    "configurations": {
      "development": {
        "optimization": false,
        "extractLicenses": false,
        "sourceMap": { "scripts": true, "styles": true, "vendor": true }
      }
    }
  },
  "serve": {
    "options": {
      "poll": 1000,
      "prebundle": { "exclude": ["libreria"] }
    }
  }
  ```

- Angular CLI cache enabled (default).

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create the app and a library (`ng new`, `ng generate library libreria`), and build the library once into `dist/libreria`.
2. In the app, add `"libreria": "file:../libreria-22/dist/libreria"` and run `npm install`.
3. In the library, create a service with a method containing `console.log('v1')`, and call it from the app's root component.
4. Run `ng build libreria --watch --configuration development` in the library, and `ng serve` in the app.
5. Change the log in the library service to `console.log('v2')` and wait until ng-packagr finishes.

**Expected:** the dev-server rebuilds and the app runs `v2`.

**Actual:** the terminal prints "Application bundle generation complete" but the app still runs `v1`. Searching `main.js` shows the old code:

```js
// ../libreria-22/dist/libreria/fesm2022/libreria.mjs
...
console.log("v1");   // old code
```

while the embedded source map has the new source:

```
sourcesContent: "... console.log('v2'); ..."
```

`dist/libreria/fesm2022/libreria.mjs` on disk does contain the new code. Stopping and restarting `ng serve` fixes it.

**Things I tried without success**

- `poll: 1000` in `serve.options` (with restart).
- Deleting `.angular/cache` and restarting (works until the next library change).
- `prebundle.exclude` with the package name.
- Starting from a shell with the drive letter in uppercase (`D:`) instead of lowercase. <remove this line if you did not launch `ng serve` from that shell>

### Minimum Reproduction

https://github.com/LuisEscamillaMartin/repro-linked-lib-stale

### Exception or Error

```text
No error. The build reports success.
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.5
Node.js           : 24.21.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.19.0
Operating System  : win32 x64
```

### Anything else relevant?

Without `preserveSymlinks`, the library is bundled into `main.js` from its real path (`../libreria-22/dist/libreria/fesm2022/libreria.mjs`), outside `node_modules`.

Issues.Title: Template diagnostics not updated in watch mode on Windows when the type-check block is unchanged
Issues.Body:
### Command serve ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description On Windows, during `ng serve`, a template edit that changes Angular diagnostics without changing the generated type-check code is not diagnosed: a stray `` (`NG5002`) still ends with "Application bundle generation complete", and `[attr.width.px]` never shows `NG8106`. Linux and `ng build` report both correctly. The resource check that invalidates `diagnosticCache` ([aot-compilation.ts#L334](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/8b26efa1ba2b922d459f88add85e7e9a9a1dd9de/packages/angular/build/src/tools/angular/compilation/aot-compilation.ts#L334)) looks up forward-slash paths from `getResourceDependencies()` in `modifiedFiles`, which holds `path.normalize`d backslash paths ([source-file-cache.ts#L42](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/8b26efa1ba2b922d459f88add85e7e9a9a1dd9de/packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/angular/source-file-cache.ts#L42)), so it never matches on Windows: ``` modifiedFiles: ["C:\\repro\\src\\app\\app.html"] resourceDependencies: ["C:/repro/src/app/app.html"] match: false (Linux: true) ``` Edits that change the `.ngtypecheck.ts` shim are still picked up by the TypeScript builder; the others rely on this check alone. A possible fix is `hostOptions.modifiedFiles.has(path.normalize(resourceDependency))`. ### Minimal Reproduction Repro: https://github.com/te-gis-dev/ng-stale-template-diagnostics (`node repro.mjs` runs all steps against `ng serve` and restores the files). With `@angular/build` 22.2.7, run `ng serve`, then: 1. Append `` to `src/app/app.html`. Expected `NG5002`; actual on Windows: build completes, no error. 2. Revert, then append `

`. Expected `NG8106` warning; actual on Windows: none. 3. Add a blank line to `src/app/app.ts`. The missing diagnostics appear. | Setup | Stray `` | `[attr.width.px]` | | --- | --- | --- | | 22.2.7, Windows 11, Node 26.12.1 | not reported | not reported | | 22.2.7, Linux (Docker `node:24`) | correct | correct | ### Exception or Error ```text Windows: Application bundle generation complete. Linux: ✘ [ERROR] NG5002: Unexpected closing tag "span". It may happen when the tag has already been closed by another tag. For more info see https://www.w3.org/TR/html5/syntax.html#closing-elements-that-have-implied-end-tags [plugin angular-compiler] Application bundle generation failed. ``` ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI : 22.2.7 Angular : 22.2.6 Node.js : 26.12.1 Package Manager : npm 11.16.0 Operating System : win32 x64 ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │ Package │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │ ├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ @angular/build │ 22.2.7 │ 22.2.7 │ │ @angular/cli │ 22.2.7 │ 22.2.7 │ │ @angular/common │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/compiler │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/compiler-cli │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/core │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/forms │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ @angular/router │ 22.2.6 │ 22.2.6 │ │ rxjs │ 7.8.2 │ ~7.8.0 │ │ typescript │ 6.0.3 │ 6.0.3 │ └───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘ ``` ### Anything else relevant? - Windows only; drive-letter casing is not involved. - Latent on `main` / 22.3.0-rc.0: #34173 marks the component affected through Angular's incremental compilation first, but the lookup is still `false` on Windows. The check has never matched there since #25940. - On 22.2.x it also locks in the stale cached error fixed by #34173: while it is served, every template edit on Windows is ignored (`repro.mjs` steps 1-6).

Issues.Title: bug(snack-bar,bottom-sheet): Idiomatic configuration not compatible with new ESLint strict type-checked rule
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

`typescript-eslint` [version 8.0.73](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/releases/tag/v8.73.0) was released on Nov 16, 2026 with a new [`no-unsafe-class-instance-assignment` rule](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/pull/12907) that flags situations where "object literal is used where an instance of class (...) is expected".

Idiomatic configuration of Snackbars or Bottom Sheets (and maybe other components) is achieved (and documented) with the use of a last parameter that falls into that case, because `MatSnackBarConfig`,  `MatBottomSheetConfig`, etc. are defined as `class` instead of `interface`.

As a consequence, a simple project with Material Angular + Typescript-ESLint project with strict type-checked linting enabled reports an error where using the components with the configuration parameter:

```typescript
snackBar.open(
  'Message archived',
  'Undo',
  { duration: 3000 } // Lint error: This object literal is used where an instance of class `MatSnackBarConfig<any>` is expected.
);
```


### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/9uwq3dhq?file=eslint.config.mjs,src%2Fmain.ts
Steps to reproduce:
1. Run `npm run lint`


### Expected Behavior

There is (presumably?) no reason to define the parameters (`MatSnackBarConfig`,  `MatBottomSheetConfig`...) as classes, interfaces should be used instead.

### Actual Behavior

Parameters are defined as classes, so the strict linting rule disallows the use of object literals.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2
- CDK/Material: 22.3
- Browser(s): N/A
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): N/A

Issues.Title: fix(material/dialog): prevent visual jump by removing open class together with closing class
Issues.Body:
When `_startExitAnimation()` is called, `mdc-dialog--open` was previously removed synchronously while `mdc-dialog--closing` was scheduled in a `requestAnimationFrame` callback.

When `close()` is called from within a `requestAnimationFrame` callback (such as during zoneless change detection scheduling or reactive effect updates), the nested rAF is deferred to the next frame. During that intermediate frame, the dialog container renders with neither class, applying the base un-opened styles (`scale(0.8)` / `opacity: 0`) and causing the dialog surface to visibly shrink and then snap back when `mdc-dialog--closing` is applied.

### Solution

Remove `mdc-dialog--open` and add `mdc-dialog--closing` together within the `requestAnimationFrame` callback so the container transitions directly from the open state to the closing state without an intermediate class-less frame. When animations are disabled, `mdc-dialog--open` is removed immediately in the non-animated branch.

### Verification

- Ran Prettier format check: passed (clean formatting).
- TypeScript compile / typecheck (`tsc -p src/material/tsconfig.json --noEmit`): clean on dialog files (0 errors).
- Added unit test in `src/material/dialog/dialog.spec.ts` asserting that `mdc-dialog--open` is not removed prematurely before the closing animation frame executes.

Fixes #34123

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/text-field): defer autosize checks until view initialization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`CdkTextareaAutosize` can cache the textarea line height during its first `ngDoCheck`, before dynamic host classes have been applied. With `matInput` inside `mat-form-field`, this means measuring the browser default font instead of the inherited font. The resulting minimum and maximum heights remain incorrect until a window resize clears the cache.

Skip automatic checks until the view has initialized, allowing the existing `ngAfterViewInit` resize to perform the initial measurement after host bindings have been applied.

For example, a textarea with a 50px line height and limits of 2–5 rows now starts with `min-height: 100px` and `max-height: 250px`.

Fixes #33944.

## Testing

Added regression tests for both a CDK textarea with a dynamic host class and a `matInput` textarea inside `mat-form-field`.

- Without the fix: both new tests fail; the existing 130 tests pass.
- With the fix: all 132 tests pass in Chromium (28 CDK text-field and 104 Material input tests).
- Existing coverage includes initial content and placeholder sizing, row limits, programmatic value changes, window resizing, and disabling/re-enabling autosize.
- Repository formatting applied to all changed files.

```sh
pnpm bazel test //src/cdk/text-field:unit_tests_chromium //src/material/input:unit_tests_chromium --test_output=errors
```

Issues.Title: bug(material/core): dark on-surface-variant uses neutral-variant 90 instead of 80
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

18.1.x

### Description

In the dark scheme, `on-surface-variant` maps to `neutral-variant` tone 90 ([`_md-sys-color.scss` L24](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/fcec64761/src/material/core/tokens/m3/_md-sys-color.scss#L24)). The Material color spec maps it to tone 80:

- [material-color-utilities `color_spec_2021.ts`](https://github.com/material-foundation/material-color-utilities/blob/main/typescript/dynamiccolor/color_spec_2021.ts): `onSurfaceVariant` → `tone: (s) => s.isDark ? 80 : 30`, unchanged since 2023.
- [material-web tokens v0_192](https://github.com/material-components/material-web/blob/main/tokens/versions/v0_192/_md-sys-color.scss): `neutral-variant80`.
- The `theme-color` schematic in this repo bundles material-color-utilities and therefore generates tone 80, so its output disagrees with the system tokens in the same package.

Tone 90 came in with #29655, which followed #29577. That issue relied on Theme Builder screenshots, and the Theme Builder labeled the dark `On Surface Var.` swatch "NV-90". That label was wrong: the swatch itself is tone 80, as already reported in material-foundation/material-theme-builder#301 (May 2024). The pixels in the screenshot attached to #29577 confirm this. The same PR changed `surface-container-highest` because of a mislabeled swatch, and #29902 reverted that change.

Because the tones are equal, `on-surface` and `on-surface-variant` render identically in the dark scheme whenever the neutral and neutral-variant palettes are close or equal. As a result, form field placeholders look like entered values, and labels and hint texts lose their visual hierarchy.

### Reproduction

No StackBlitz reproduction: the wrong value is a static token mapping and can be read directly in [`_md-sys-color.scss` L24](https://github.com/angular/components/blob/fcec64761/src/material/core/tokens/m3/_md-sys-color.scss#L24).

To see the effect:

1. Generate a theme with `ng generate @angular/material:theme-color` and the same color for neutral and neutral-variant, e.g. `#ececed`.
2. Render a `mat-form-field` with `appearance="outline"`, a placeholder and `floatLabel="always"`, next to a filled one, in the dark scheme.

### Expected Behavior

`--mat-sys-on-surface-variant` resolves to `neutral-variant` tone 80 in the dark scheme. Placeholders are visibly dimmer than entered values.

### Actual Behavior

`--mat-sys-on-surface-variant` resolves to tone 90, the same tone as `--mat-sys-on-surface`. Placeholders and values are indistinguishable.

### Environment

- Angular Material: 22.2.6
- Still present on `main` (fcec64761)

Issues.Title: Autocomplete can select an option after being disabled while open
Issues.Body:
### Reproduction

1. Attach an Angular Material autocomplete with Apple and Orange options to a reactive form input. Start with Apple selected.
2. Use a timer to call `control.disable()` in two seconds. Focus the input before the timer fires so the panel opens.
3. After the input is disabled, click Orange in the panel.

The input changes to Orange and `optionSelected` fires. The same happens if the timer sets `matAutocompleteDisabled` to true instead.

Disabling either the form control or autocomplete should close the existing suggestions without selecting an option. With `matAutocompleteDisabled`, the user should still be able to type in the plain input.

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/scrolling): prevent nested tables from inheriting outer viewport
Issues.Body:
Hi! This fixes ordinary tables inside `*cdkVirtualFor` items throwing `CdkVirtualScrollViewport is already attached.` on initial render.

Fixes #34121.

### What changes

An inner table can resolve the outer `CDK_VIRTUAL_SCROLL_VIEWPORT` token and enable table virtualization, even though `cdkVirtualFor` already owns that viewport.

Provide `null` for this token on `CdkVirtualForOf`, alongside the existing `VIRTUAL_SCROLLABLE` boundary introduced in #34100. This lets tables inside the repeated items render normally. The repeater itself resolves its owning viewport using `skipSelf`, and an independent nested viewport provides its own token.

This also means custom consumers of `CDK_VIRTUAL_SCROLL_VIEWPORT` inside virtual-for items resolve `null` instead of implicitly inheriting the outer viewport.

### Regression coverage

Add a test with ordinary tables inside virtual-for items. It checks that each table renders all of its rows without virtual-table fixed layout, both initially and after scrolling. It also checks that the outer viewport retains the correct data length and advances its rendered range.

Before the fix, the new test fails with the reported error; the other 89 CDK table tests pass.

### Validation

Completed locally:

- CDK table: Chromium (90 passed) and Firefox (90 passed).
- CDK scrolling: Chromium (109 passed).
- Material table: Chromium (36 passed).
- Repository formatter, targeted TSLint, and `git diff --check`.

The standalone reproduction linked in #34121 was also verified in Chrome using published Angular/CDK 22.2.6.
